extracted.intended_audience: regulatory practitioners, labor law attorneys, agency staff, labor unions, employers, and public stakeholders monitoring labor-management rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: An index/listing of Federal Register documents and abstracts relating to labor-management relations rulemakings, corrections, and procedural changes. Useful for tracking substantive rule changes (e.g., joint-employer tests, employee/independent-contractor analysis) and procedural filing/service requirements for FLRA, NLRB, DOL, FMCS, and related agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint employer status determination under the FLSA/FMLA/MSPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify how to determine joint employer status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) in Part 791 and amend FMLA and MSPA provisions to determine joint employer status using the Department's FLSA analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clarity and a measure of uniformity for employers and employees; offer a nationwide standard for investigators and enforcement personnel to ensure evenhanded application, preserve core consistency with relevant judicial frameworks, marshal commonality between approaches closest to the statute, simplify enforcement, reduce litigation, and provide a reliable uniform analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee vs. independent contractor status analysis under the FLSA/FMLA/MSPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind the analysis currently in 29 CFR part 795 and replace it with the analysis published and adopted in the Department's January 7, 2021 final rule (with a few modifications); apply this analysis to the FMLA and MSPA, which incorporate the FLSA's employment definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernize and unify the test used to determine employee or independent contractor status across statutes that incorporate FLSA definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual inflation adjustment of civil monetary penalties (Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must annually adjust civil monetary penalties for inflation no later than January 15 of each year using a cost-of-living formula specified by the Inflation Adjustment Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments are required notwithstanding section 553 of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA); final rules set forth the Department's annual adjustments and the adjusted penalty levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLRA representation proceedings: provide decisions on all consequential issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise regulations governing representation proceedings to provide parties in most cases with decisions from the Authority on all consequential issues in representation proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes are intended to optimize the FLRA's workforce by streamlining decision-making, consistent with E.O. 14,210; certain parts may be interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of agency organization, procedure, or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update FLRA/FSIP methods for obtaining and filing forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish revised methods by which the public may obtain specific forms from the Federal Service Impasses Panel (FSIP) and then file or formally submit those forms and other documents during FSIP proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative update to access and submission procedures to reflect revised methods (no substantive change to merits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing deadline phrasing and timezone specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronically filed (eFiled) documents must be filed electronically by '11:59 p.m.' rather than 'midnight' on the due date, and specify that the 11:59 p.m. filing deadline is 'Eastern Time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical clarification to remove ambiguity about filing cutoffs and time zone for deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional email service for Authority documents (FLRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit parties to proceedings before the FLRA's three-Member decisional component to voluntarily request—in individual cases filed through the FLRA's eFiling system—that the Authority use electronic mail (email) to serve the requesting parties any decisions, orders, and notices issued in those individual cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary option; adopted (in some documents) without change; agency welcomes comments in interim-final instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person filing appointment requirement (FLRA CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties wish to file documents with the FLRA's Office of Case Intake and Publication (CIP) in person, they must schedule an appointment at least one business day in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor procedural requirement designed to manage in-person intake; adopted with minor technical changes in some instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of four-copy filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend regulations to eliminate the requirement that parties file four copies of original documents with the FLRA's Authority, Office of the General Counsel (OGC), and FLRA Administrative Law Judges, Regional Directors, and Hearing Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update to streamline filing burdens and modernize filing practice (administrative/formatting change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of cross-references in representation-case procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct previously published representation-case procedure regulations that failed to update certain cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical corrections to ensure internal regulatory consistency; does not change substantive procedures except by correcting references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission or restoration of representation-case procedure provisions in response to court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind or restore specific provisions of representation-case procedures to comply with court decisions (e.g., rescission of four provisions vacated by D.C. Circuit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency rulemaking can implement judicial decisions by removing or restoring regulatory text; such changes are framed as effectuating appropriate policy choices to enhance fair, efficient, and expeditious resolution of cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMCS terms of service and confidentiality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set forth terms for the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service's provision of services to clients, including rules expounding upon confidentiality associated with FMCS's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines service terms and confidentiality expectations for mediation/conciliation clients; governs how FMCS will provide and protect information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous technical, formatting, and administrative updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt minor or technical changes to regulations (e.g., update addresses and telephone numbers; change phrasing from 'midnight' to '11:59 p.m.'; specify Eastern Time; minor formatting changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These adjustments are administrative in nature, often adopted without substantive change, intended to improve clarity and align regulatory text with current practices.
